extra.message: The 'password' parameter from params (user-supplied) is concatenated directly into a SQL string via cursor.execute(). cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command (SQL Injection)

extra.message: User-supplied 'comment' parameter is inserted directly into an INSERT SQL statement via string formatting. This allows SQL injection in the comment field, which is later displayed to other users, creating a stored SQL injection vector as well.

extra.message: User-supplied 'comment' value from params is reflected back in the HTML response without any HTML encoding. An attacker can store a script payload via the comment parameter, which will be served to any user who views the comments, resulting in a stored (persistent) XSS vulnerability.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: User-controlled input from URL hash fragment is written directly to the page via document.write() inside the HTML_PREFIX template. The fragment (?lang=...) contains attacker-controlled content that is decoded and injected into the DOM unencoded, enabling cross-site scripting.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The user can supply any integer 'id' parameter in the SQL query to retrieve arbitrary user records (id, username, name, surname, password) without any authentication check on this endpoint. There is no authorization logic to ensure the requested user belongs to the current session.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key (Insecure Direct Object Reference)

extra.message: The 'path' query parameter is passed to os.path.abspath() and then directly to open() without any path traversal validation. An attacker can use '../' sequences to read arbitrary files on the server (e.g. /etc/passwd) or use URLs to fetch resources from arbitrary external locations.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: User-supplied 'domain' parameter is concatenated directly into an os.system-style command string via subprocess.run with shell=True. An attacker can execute arbitrary system commands by injecting shell metacharacters in the 'domain' parameter.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: When '://' is found in the 'path' parameter, urllib.request.urlopen() is called with the user-supplied value. This enables Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF), allowing an attacker to make the server fetch arbitrary resources, including internal network endpoints.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: User-supplied 'xml' parameter is parsed by lxml.etree.parse() with load_dtd=True and resolve_entities=True. This enables XML External Entity (XXE) attacks allowing an attacker to read local files (e.g. /etc/passwd), perform SSRF against internal services, or cause denial of service via entity-based DoS.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE)

extra.message: User-supplied 'name' parameter is interpolated directly into an XPath query string via string formatting. An attacker can inject arbitrary XPath expressions to enumerate user data or bypass name-based filtering in USERS_XML.

extra.message: The 'include' parameter is fetched via urllib.request.urlopen() when the value contains '://', then its contents are executed via exec(), which runs arbitrary Python code supplied by the attacker on the server. This is a Remote Code Execution (RCE) via Remote File Inclusion (RFI).

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The 'include' parameter is opened via open() when not using '://' URLs. The file contents are then executed via exec() on line 57. This allows Local File Inclusion (LFI) followed by arbitrary Python code execution, resulting in Remote Code Execution (RCE).

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The 'path' parameter is passed to open() with os.path.abspath() applied. While abspath() normalizes the path, it does not prevent traversal to files outside the intended directory. extra.message: The 'object' query parameter is directly passed to pickle.loads() without any validation. An attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload to achieve arbitrary code execution on the server (Remote Code Execution).
